question: Why are Veda-declared actions said to be insufficient for mortals' desired accomplishment?
premises: Actions declared in the Veda are named as the means.
Mortals are the agents in question.
They are said not to be capable of accomplishing what they desire by those actions.
inference: Mortals are not capable of accomplishing their desired ends through Veda-declared actions alone.
uncertainties: The reason for this incapacity is not stated in this unit.
plain_english: Mortals are not capable of accomplishing what they desire by means of the actions declared in the Veda.
